sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:182071
Court No. - 73
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 5706 of 2023

Applicant :- Faizuddin
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 2 Others

Counsel for Applicant :- Deepak Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Irshad Ahmad
Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.
1. Apprehending his arrest in Complaint Case No.3282 of 2022 (Muskan Vs. Faizuddin) under
Sections 376, 506 Ipc, Police Station Amroha Dehat, District Amroha, the present anticipatory bail
application has been moved on behalf of the applicant - Faizuddin.
2.  In the revised list, none present on behalf of the complainant.
Learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State are present.

3. A criminal complaint case was lodged by the complainant / victim against the present applicant alleging therein that the marriage between the two was settled and on the basis of that the present applicant made physical relations with the victim against her will and when it was disclosed to the family members of the victim, they negotiated with the applicant and his family members to perform the marriage, but they flatly refused.

A criminal complaint was filed before the court and after completing the necessary formalities, a summoning order was passed on 19.11.2022 against the applicant before the Magistrate Court to face trial under sections 376, 506 IPC.

entities.text: Faizuddin vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
There is no credible evidence against him.
Allegations levelled against the applicant are false.

It is further submitted that no rape was committed with the prosecutrix of the case by the applicant and as a matter of fact, with the mutual consent of the family members of both the parties, the relationship was broken and the gifts received from either side were returned to each other and a compromise also took place before the police of Police Station Kotwali Amroha on 13.9.2022.
It is further submitted that no place of occurrence has been disclosed in the complaint and even in the evidence on record.

It is further submitted that a process under section 82 Cr.P.C.
has wrongly been issued by the court against the applicant after passing the summoning order.

It is further submitted that earlier, interim protection was granted to the applicant by way of interim anticipatory bail vide order dated 19.5.2023 passed by this Court and the said liberty was never misused by the applicant.
It is further submitted that no offence is made out against the applicant on the basis of evidence available on record and as such he is entitled for anticipatory bail.

5. Per contra, learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail and it has been vehemently submitted that on the basis of cogent and sufficient evidence, the learned Magistrate has summoned the applicant to face trial under section 376, 506 IPC.

Since the marriage between the parties was settled, the applicant taking benefit of this situation and of the innocence of the prosecutrix as well made physical relations with her against her will and thus committed offence of rape and subsequently the applicant refused to perform marriage with the prosecutrix.

It is further submitted that on the false promise of marriage, only to fulfill his lust, the applicant made physical relations with the prosecutrix and subsequently did not keep his promise and refused to marry her.

It is further submitted that no compromise, as alleged by the applicant, ever took place between the two families nor any compromise takes part of the case diary and all such story is false and forged.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and the seriousness of the offence, the applicant is not entitled to get any relief by way of anticipatory bail by this Court and the present applicant is liable to be rejected.

6. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and considering the documents available on record, the attention of the Court was drawn towards the paragraph no.14 of the affidavit annexed with the present application wherein it has been averred that the applicant does not want to marry at present, as he wants to prepare his future.
It is further deposed in the said paragraph that the family members of the victim are still pressuring him to perform marriage with the victim.
This averment on part of applicant shows that since the very inception, he never intended to marry with the victim and he was only fulfilling his lust.

7. Unfortunately, not only the Courts now a days are over-flooded with a large number of cases of such type wherein it is alleged that the male accused, on the false promise of marriage, only to fulfill his lust, made physical relations with the victim and subsequently did not keep his promise and left her abandoned, but the delicate matters of such nature are also leading to affect the harmony of the society.
In such matters, what the Court should actually look into is the intention of the accused from very inception of the relation.

sentences.text:
Hon'ble Apex Court in Pramod Suryabhan Pawar Vs. The State of Maharashtra & Anr., 2019 (9)
SCC 608 has categorically held that there is a distinction between a false promise given on understanding by maker that it will be broken and breach of a promise which is made in good faith but subsequently not fulfilled.

entities.text:
Pramod Suryabhan Pawar Vs. The State of Maharashtra & Anr., 2019 (9)
SCC 608
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In paragraph 14 of the aforesaid judgment, the Hon'ble Apex Court held that :
"14. ...
In the present case, the "misconception of fact" alleged by the complainant is the appellant's promise to marry her.

Specifically in the context of a promise to marry, this Court has observed that there is a distinction between a false promise given on the understanding by the maker that it will be broken, and the breach of a promise which is made in good faith but subsequently not fulfilled.

In Anurag Soni v State of Chhattisgarh, (2019) SCC OnLine SC 509, this Court held:
"37.

entities.text: Anurag Soni v State of Chhattisgarh, (2019) SCC OnLine SC 509
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The sum and substance of the aforesaid decisions would be that if it is established and proved that from the inception the accused who gave the promise to the prosecutrix to marry, did not have any intention to marry and the prosecutrix gave the consent for sexual intercourse on such an assurance by the accused that he would marry her, such a consent can be said to be a consent obtained on a misconception of fact as per Section 90 of the IPC and, in such a case, such a consent would not excuse the offender and such an offender can be said to have committed the rape as defined under Section 375 of the IPC and can be convicted for the offence under Section 376 of the IPC."
9.

Similar observations were made by this Court in Deepak Gulati v State of Haryana, (2013) 7 SCC 675 ("Deepak Gulati"):
"21.

entities.text: Deepak Gulati v State of Haryana, (2013) 7 SCC 675
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is a distinction between the mere breach of a promise, and not fulfilling a false promise.
Thus, the court must examine whether there was made, at an early stage a false promise of marriage by the accused"

Further, in paragraph 16 of the aforesaid judgment explaining the terms - misconception of fact,
consent and breach of promise, the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that :
"16. ...

Where the promise to marry is false and the intention of the maker at the time of making the promise itself was not to abide by it but to deceive the woman to convince her to engage in sexual relations, there is a "misconception of fact" that vitiates the woman's "consent".
On the other hand, a breach of a promise cannot be said to be a false promise.
To establish a false promise, the maker of the promise should have had no intention of upholding his word at the time of giving it.
The "consent" of a woman under Section 375 is vitiated on the ground of a "misconception of fact" where such misconception was the basis for her choosing to engage in the said act.

In Deepak Gulati this Court observed:

3 "21.

entities.text: Faizuddin vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is a distinction between the mere breach of a promise, and not fulfilling a false promise.

Thus, the court must examine whether there was made, at an early stage a false promise of marriage by the accused; and whether the consent involved was given after wholly understanding the nature and consequences of sexual indulgence.

There may be a case where the prosecutrix agrees to have sexual intercourse on account of her love and passion for the accused, and not solely on account of misrepresentation made to her by the accused, or where an accused on account of circumstances which he could not have foreseen, or which were beyond his control, was unable to marry her, despite having every intention to do so.
Such cases must be treated differently.

24. Hence, it is evident that there must be adequate evidence to show that at the relevant time i.e. at the initial stage itself, the accused had no intention whatsoever,
of keeping his promise to marry the victim.

There may, of course, be circumstances,
when a person having the best of intentions is unable to marry the victim owing to various unavoidable circumstances.
The "failure to keep a promise made with respect to a future uncertain date, due to reasons that are not very clear from the evidence available, does not always amount to misconception of fact.
In order to come within the meaning of the term "misconception of fact", the fact must have an immediate relevance".

Section 90 IPC cannot be called into aid in such a situation, to pardon the act of a girl in entirety, and fasten criminal liability on the other, unless the court is assured of the fact that from the very beginning, the accused had never really intended to marry her."
(Emphasis supplied)

10. In the present case, it reflects from the factual matrix of the matter that the physical relations between the victim and the accused developed on the basis of a promise to marry on the part of the accused applicant despite the protest of the victim and against her wishes, which continued for many occasions, but subsequently the accused applicant flatly refused to marry her.
Specific averment has also been made in the affidavit filed by the accused applicant that he does not want to marry the victim.
In this way the promise to marry was broken by the accused applicant himself.
Exploiting the victim on the pretext of marriage and finally refusing to marry her are such tendencies growing in the society, which must be nipped in the bud.
It is a serious offence against the society, hence the applicant is not entitled to any indulgence.

11. Since it is a complaint case and the applicant has been summoned on the basis of the statements made by the complainant and the witnesses under Sections 200 and 202 Cr.P.C. respectively and as per law laid down in Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1, the anticipatory bail application is maintainable and the same may be granted in a complaint case also

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
, in the same law, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that while considering an application for grant of anticipatory bail, the court has to consider the nature of the offence, the role of the person,
the likelihood of his influencing the course of investigation, or tampering with evidence including intimidating witnesses, likelihood of fleeing justice, such as leaving the country, etc.

It has further been held that Courts ought to be generally guided by considerations such as the nature and gravity of the offences, the role attributed to the applicant, and the facts of the case, while considering Faizuddin vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163400838/

sentences.text: whether to grant anticipatory bail, or refuse it.
Whether to grant or not is a matter of discretion.

12. Hence, considering the settled principles of law regarding anticipatory bail, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, role of applicant and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion of the merits of the case, in my view, it is not a fit case for anticipatory bail to the applicant till the end of the trial.
13. The anticipatory bail application is rejected.
